title: Afreximbank's $5bn Caribbean Push and the Africa–CARICOM Partnership | The Six, Ep. 13
lede: Africa and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) — the African Union's self-declared Sixth Region — are building a partnership in trade finance, direct flights and reparations diplomacy. Afreximbank has raised its Caribbean financing cap from $3 billion to $5 billion, a new UN resolution has put reparations on the table, and the first direct Lagos–Barbados flight began in May 2026. This episode maps where the money, the planes and the politics actually stand.
keyPoints: Afreximbank raised its CARICOM financing cap from US$3 billion to US$5 billion in February 2026, with more than US$750 million disbursed, a pipeline above US$2 billion, and 13 CARICOM states acceded to the bank; it runs a Caribbean office in Bridgetown, Barbados (Afreximbank; Ecofin Agency).

CARICOM groups 15 member states and about 18.5 million people; the AU treats it as the diaspora's Sixth Region. The two blocs held their first summit online in September 2021, named 7 September Africa-CARICOM Day, signed an AU–CARICOM MoU in September 2024, and met in person in Addis Ababa in September 2025 (Caribbean Community; Jamaica Observer).

A UN General Assembly resolution written by Ghana, adopted on 25 March 2026, called the transatlantic slave trade one of the gravest crimes against humanity and urged dialogue on reparations; it passed 123–3 (US and Israel against) with 52 abstentions (Al Jazeera).

An ITC–Afreximbank report (3 Nov 2026) found about 80% of Africa's goods-export potential to the Caribbean is untapped and put combined trade potential at up to US$1.65 billion a year by 2030. Nigeria's Air Peace flew the first direct Lagos–Barbados service in May 2026 (Boeing 777), now twice monthly (ITC/Afreximbank; Caribbean360).

The fourth AfriCaribbean Trade and Investment Forum (ACTIF2025) in Grenada closed with over US$300 million in deals and delegates from 80 countries; ACTIF2026, set for St. Kitts in July, was deferred over a public-health alert in parts of Africa. Ghana's President Mahama is set to chair the AU in 2027 and wants to link the AfCFTA to the Caribbean (Afreximbank; Graphic Online).
